Welcome to Bladon Church of England Primary School . . .
Where faith inspires us, wisdom grows and every child is encouraged to shine.
I knew from the very first time I visited Bladon many years ago, that it was a truly special place. Ours is a small school with a big heart – a place where every child is known, valued and encouraged to flourish. It is something you will notice the moment you walk through our doors.
At the heart of everything we do is our Christian vision:
Rooted in faith, growing in wisdom, shining in life
Together, we nurture curiosity, inspire creativity and embrace the world with confidence, compassion and hope.
Inspired by Jesus’ words in Matthew 5:16,
“Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.”
our vision shapes every aspect of school life. We want every child to develop deep roots of faith, belonging and character, to grow in wisdom through rich learning and meaningful experiences and to shine brightly by using their unique gifts to make a positive difference in the world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Welcome – Bladon CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Bladon Church of England Primary School . . .
Where faith inspires us, wisdom grows and every child is encouraged to shine.
I knew from the very first time I visited Bladon many years ago, that it was a truly special place. Ours is a small school with a big heart – a place where every child is known, valued and encouraged to flourish. It is something you will notice the moment you walk through our doors.
At the heart of everything we do is our Christian vision:
Rooted in faith, growing in wisdom, shining in life
Together, we nurture curiosity, inspire creativity and embrace the world with confidence, compassion and hope.
Inspired by Jesus’ words in Matthew 5:16,
“Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.”
our vision shapes every aspect of school life. We want every child to develop deep roots of faith, belonging and character, to grow in wisdom through rich learning and meaningful experiences and to shine brightly by using their unique gifts to make a positive difference in the world.
As a Church of England school, we believe that every child is uniquely created and deeply valued by God. We are committed to providing an education that enables children to flourish academically, spiritually, socially and emotionally within a caring and inclusive Christian community.
Learning at Bladon is about far more than acquiring knowledge. We nurture curiosity, encourage creativity and inspire children to think deeply, ask questions and embrace new challenges with confidence. We believe children learn best through a broad, ambitious and engaging curriculum that values every subject and enables every child to discover their talents and interests.
We encourage our children to persevere when learning is challenging, to take responsibility for their choices, to show compassion towards others and to recognise that everyone has something valuable to contribute. We want our children to leave us not only with excellent academic foundations, but with the wisdom, hope and confidence to flourish in the next stage of their lives and beyond.
Our dedicated staff embody this vision every day, creating an environment where children feel safe, inspired and loved. Together with our families, governors, church and wider community, we work in partnership so that every child can put down strong roots, continue growing throughout their journey and let their light shine.
We are fortunate to be situated in a beautiful village within an area of outstanding natural beauty. We continually work to make the very best of our unique setting in order to provide an intimate, nurturing environment in which our children can thrive.
The pages of our website are designed to give you a glimpse into life at Bladon C of E Primary School, and the spirit, energy and enjoyment which make it such a special place.
Please do get in touch to arrange a visit, we would be delighted to show you around our wonderful school.
Vickie Cook
Headteacher's Welcome

What is the Woodstock Partnership?
The Partnership is a collection of local schools that work together in many ways. The schools involved are: Woodstock, Tackley, Stonesfield, Combe, Bletchingdon, William Fletcher and The Marlborough School. We regularly take part in Partnership sports events giving the children the opportunity to compete against other schools.
Our staff attend network meetings, sharing ideas and offering opportunities to moderate work across a wider group.

Beyond the Curriculum
Intent
At Bladon C of E Primary School, we provide many enrichment opportunities across our curriculum to enhance the learning experiences of our children. Our topic-based approach enables links to be made in the local community such as Blenheim Palace, Woodstock Museum, the Ashmolean Museum as well as further afield in Oxfordshire. We want to widen children’s experiences as they go through our school, becoming life-long learners and global citizens.
Implementation
Church connections
Teachers plan purposeful learning opportunities that widen the children’s experiences and build on their skills and knowledge. As a Church of England School, we focus on many key events in the Christian calendar. Whole-school Harvest and Easter services allow the children to participate in our local Church services which promote the Christian Values and provide the children with a sense of community and belonging. At Christmas time, our younger children take part in a Nativity in which they all help to retell the Christmas Story. Our older children take part in a Carol Concert and share the Christmas story through narration and song. Reverend Katie leads a weekly collective worship within school as well as being an active member of our school community. He has worked with our school worship team to deliver child-led collective worship.
Leadership and community roles
We feel it is important to offer our children leadership roles to help build their confidence and self-esteem as representatives of not only their class, but also the school. The children have several opportunities to take on responsibility and work collaboratively with children as well as adults.
Every child who joins Bladon CE Primary School is allocated to one of our four houses all named after local rivers: Cherwell (Red), Evenlode (Yellow), Glyme (Green) and Windrush (Blue). Children in Years 5 and 6 then are given the chance to deliver a speech to the school about why they feel they should be house captain or vice-captain. The rest of the school then vote on the roles. Each week Dojo points are totalled by house and a cup is presented the captain of the house who has won the most points that week.
Children in Years 1-6 have the chance to become members of the School Council each year. They are elected in the Autumn term by their peers. The School Council has organised charity events and been part of the interview panel for new members of staff.
The worship team is comprised of children from Years 1-6 and they come together to plan their own worship assemblies with support from staff or the local Reverend.
We believe physical education is another great way to develop leadership skills in our children. This is why we offer the opportunity for children in Years 5 and 6 to apply for the role of playground leader. Any child who is interested is encouraged to write a short note explaining why they feel they would be good for the role and what skills and behaviours they would bring. Successful leaders then support at playtimes, on a rota, setting out equipment, ensuring it is used correctly, helping younger children to enjoy their playtimes and facilitate some structured games.
National Events
We promote awareness of national events such as Remembrance Day, Anti-Bullying Week, World Mental Health Day, European Day of Languages, Safer Internet Day and World Book Day. Through these events we help enable our children to discover their roles as a Global Citizen.
After school clubs and music
We offer a range of after-school activities in addition to the normal after-school club provision on offer.
There is a sports club three days a week from 3-4:00pm and these change from term to term to reflect the demand for an individual sport, the season and the sports being taught through the curriculum. Most after-school sports take place at the excellent all-weather facilities we have use of off-site.
Over the years, staff with different interests and expertise have led a range of other clubs including art club, creative writing and book club.
We have two external companies who use the site for after-school provision too, giving our children the opportunity to learn karate and musical theatre.
Our most popular club is choir on a Wednesday from September to January. The children learn a wide range of songs to prepare for the Young Voices concert at Birmingham Arena. On the concert day, they join with around 6,000 other children as a single choir supported by a live band and a range of guest artists. It is one of the highlights of the school calendar for those who take part!
We use specialist teachers from the Oxfordshire Music Service to provide most of our music curriculum. Children in Chestnut Class learn recorders and children in Maple Class learn brass. There is also the option for parents to pay for additional music lessons. We currently have children who enjoy piano, violin and drum lessons.
School trips and residentials
To enhance the curriculum and further develop their love of learning, all children are given the opportunity to go on school trips and residentials, ensuring their school experience is filled with opportunity, positivity, and memorable moments. This helps them to gain real world experiences that cannot be taught in the classroom as well as opening their minds to different cultures and strengthening their knowledge of the world around them. When our Year 6 children come to write their leaving speeches, they often mention when they went to visit the Ashmolean, Woodstock Museum, Oxford Castle, Story Museum and talks and workshops by experts in their fields. Children in Acorn class also participate in weekly Forest School sessions on site. We believe that it is important to develop children’s independence and confidence in staying away from home, and so we have carefully planned class experiences to build on these skills gradually through their time at Bladon.
Impact
We may be a small school, but we believe in offering our children a wealth of experiences beyond the curriculum which give them treasured memories of their time at primary school. These experiences enable our children to leave Bladon as well-rounded individuals with valuable skills that are transferable in many aspects of their lives. They build their resilience, social skills and ability to work as a team. Bladon children become compassionate, independent thinkers and learners with passion and drive who are proud of their individuality.
Enrichment

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Information – Bladon CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
“Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.”
Statement of Intent
At Bladon Primary School, we strive to ensure every child can achieve the highest standards possible through an inclusive and inspiring curriculum. Our school curriculum is underpinned by the values that we adhere to at Bladon Church of England Primary School. The curriculum is the means by which the school achieves its objective of educating children in the knowledge, skills and understanding that they need in order to lead fulfilling lives. Our Values are: Friendship, Resilience, Respect, Equity, Compassion and Responsibility. Our values run over a two-year programme, as we endeavour to look at each one in depth and ensure that they are embedded in everyday life, both in school and outside. With Christian values at the heart, we offer a stimulating and inspiring learning experience for all. We value each child as an individual and nurture their potential for learning with a high-quality topic-based curriculum to ensure they are prepared for their continuing learning journey.
As a small village school we are able to foster a motivating and creative curriculum that engages with the local community and accesses first hand learning opportunities to inspire and motivate. We are very proud to have strong partnerships with parents to ensure their child is always supported and given the opportunity to thrive.
Our curriculum is intended to:
Implementation
Through high quality teaching of knowledge, skills and vocabulary across core and foundation subjects, all children are challenged to be inquisitive, compassionate, courageous and creative learners. They have opportunities to influence their own learning through age-appropriate and progressive themes and topics. Effective learning characteristics including being ambitious, reflective and imaginative, which will drive teaching and learning, as well as passion, praise and enthusiasm.
Senior Leaders and Governors ensure we all work in a strong and supportive environment, with the children’s education underpinning everything we do. Teachers have a clear progression of skills which structures the delivery and assessment of each subject. Each subject has an experienced Lead and a commitment to constantly improving their practice.
We are proud to offer specialist teaching in Music and PE which ensures we can provide a thorough and in-depth subject knowledge across these Foundation subjects. High quality PSHE teaching allows for an individual’s personal development, as well as enrichment opportunities such as Art Week, The Big Science Event, Residential, Young Voices and school trips that all contribute to a child being a successful learner.
The school aims to foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not share it by:
• Promoting tolerance, friendship and understanding of a range of religions and cultures through different aspects of our curriculum. This includes teaching in RE, citizenship, and Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education, but also activities in other curriculum areas. For example, as part of teaching and learning in English/reading, children will be introduced to literature from a range of cultures
• Holding assemblies dealing with relevant issues. Children will be encouraged to take a lead in such assemblies and we will also invite external speakers to contribute
• Working with our local community. This includes inviting leaders of local faith groups to speak at assemblies, and organising school trips and activities based around the local community
• Encouraging and implementing initiatives to deal with tensions between different groups of children within the school. For example, our school council has representatives from different year groups and is formed of children from a range of backgrounds. All children are encouraged to participate in the school’s activities, such as sports clubs. We also work with parents to promote knowledge and understanding of different cultures
Impact
At Bladon Primary School we pride ourselves on a happy and safe school, where children are able to thrive and feel safe and cared for. Teachers and staff work hard to plan a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum to ensure their school experience is filled with opportunity, positivity and memorable moments.
We proudly recognise not just academic ability, but also sporting, musical and creative achievements. The amount of opportunities children have access to at Bladon is exceptional for such a small village school. We are proud to have a high level of participation in after school clubs and sporting events.
When leaving Bladon Primary School at the end of Year 6, we want to ensure children are ready for the next step in their educational journey and are well-placed to make a positive contribution to society. As learners, children will have a secure disciplinary and substantive knowledge base in all subjects across the primary curriculum. They will demonstrate critical thinking skills, resilience and will have a love of learning which will set them up to be lifelong learners. As citizens in their community and the wider world, children will value individuality and self-expression, both in themselves and others, and will demonstrate tolerance and friendship towards all, regardless of individual differences.
Curriculum Provision

Testimonials
Every morning, pupils walk excitedly through the school gates, bringing with them a tangible anticipation of what the day will hold. They look forward to learning in this safe and nurturing environment. Relationships between staff and pupils are warm and congenial.
Leaders have high expectations. The school’s values of ‘respect, responsibility, compassion, friendship, perseverance and equality’ are lived and breathed by adults and pupils alike. Pupils bring joy to the village by taking an active part in special celebrations at the nearby church.
There is a calm and purposeful atmosphere in lessons. Pupils are polite to others. They follow instructions with thought and care. Pupils routinely invite feedback from their peers to help them improve their work. The curriculum is interesting and ambitious.
Staff are unequivocally proud to work here. They talk about the strong team spirit. Staff agree that leaders value their views and are supportive of their workload and well-being. Highly skilled governors understand their responsibilities well. Governors know exactly what needs to improve further in the quality of education.
Staff, governors and families work together to provide the highest standards of learning, where all are respected. Staff and governors endeavour to create a family ethos underpinned by the Christian vision and values.
Pupils share the school vision and the difference Christian values make to their behaviour and responsibility to the wider world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship – Bladon CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
What is collective worship?
Collective worship in schools should aim to provide the opportunity for pupils and staff
to worship God
to consider spiritual and moral issues
to explore their own beliefs
to develop community spirit
What do we mean by ‘worship’ at Bladon CE Primary School?
We believe in coming together as a school, Key Stages or as individual classes to: –
Celebrate and appreciate
Contemplate and wonder
Inspire and enthuse
Be comfortable and nourished
Be thankful and pray
Focus and content of worship
Collective worship is seen as a rich opportunity to provide for pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development. For this to be successful worship should:
Following the call to worship there are various ways of gathering. Assembling in silence, singing a well-known song, listening to music, watching a looped slide show are all examples. As part of the gathering, a greeting is used to welcome everyone and to make a beginning to our worship establishing the liturgical pattern.
At Bladon CE Primary School, we open an act of worship with
Collective worship may be led by the Headteacher, local Reverend (weekly), teaching staff or the child-led worship team.
Have a sense of occasion
Invite participation
Be concerned with the worship of God
Celebrate beliefs, values and ideals
Promote Christian moral values
Foster a sense of community and belonging
Celebrate pupils’ talents
Make use of symbols and imagery
Our School Prayer
That working together and playing together,
We may learn to serve you and to serve one another,
Our Christian Vision and Values
These are an important feature of our collective worship. Our Christian Vision at Bladon is:
Flourish as a family in the fullness of life. Feed the Mind; free the Imagination.
“But the godly shall flourish like palm trees and grow tall as the cedars of Lebanon. For they are transplanted into the Lord’s own garden and are under his personal care. Even in old age they will still produce fruit and be vital and green. This honours the Lord and exhibits his faithful care. He is my shelter. There is nothing but goodness in him!” Psalm 12.15.
Together as a family, feeding the mind with knowledge and understanding, fostering feelings of awe and wonder about the world in which we live, so that children flourish, living life in all its fullness. The expectation is that everyone who is part of our school will always try their very best, enjoying and thriving on the challenges that new learning brings. Our values of friendship, resilience, respect, equity, compassion and responsibility are implicit in everything we do and are demonstrated in every aspect of school life. The children were involved in choosing the values we promote at Bladon and regularly share their thoughts and ideas on how best to demonstrate them. The vision and values are inspired by Biblical themes which resonate with the whole school community and are reinforced and discussed in collective worship.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Resilience Award – Bladon CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Resilience Mission Statement:
Working together to build resilient minds for overcoming adversity, lifelong learning and enduring friendships
Our ultimate ambition for the children in our care is to nurture their personal qualities, which will enable them to flourish and continue to grow during the next stage of their education journey and beyond. The importance of resilience in children’s growth as learners and as people cannot be overestimated. Possessing resilience provides a secure foundation when seeking out and engaging with new challenges, learning as they do. Developing these qualities in our children will also have a positive impact on their experience of primary school life, as learners, as classmates, as friends and as positive contributors to school life and the wider community.
With this in mind, we are delighted to be working towards achieving the Pupil Resilience School Impact Award (Silver) which is designed to recognise our work as a school community to foster resilience in our children. Initially, we are focusing on 4 strands but there is scope for focusing on further areas and achieving a Gold award. The current strands we are focusing on are:
Promoting resilience through the school ethos and culture
Embedding the language of resilience across the school
Promoting digital resilience
Encouraging a growth mindset approach
